[[Category:Large language models]]
[[Category:Natural language processing]]
A '''large language model''' ('''LLM''') is an [[artificial neural network (ANN)]] with a very large parameter count, trained by [[machine learning]] on broad text corpora to model the distribution of token sequences, so that it can generate text in response to a prompt.

== Architecture ==

The dominant architecture at the time of writing (2026-11) is the [[autoregressive decoder-only Transformer]].<ref>{{#cite:Q3130}}</ref> 

== Scaling laws ==

The performance of LLMs improves predictably with

* model size
* training-data volume
* computational budget

[[Language model loss]] and [[Chinchilla prescription]] describe the correlation.<ref>{{#cite:Q3141}}</ref><ref>{{#cite:Q3164}}</ref>

== Inference ==

With [[tokenisation (machine learning)#Definition|token vocabulary]] $\mathcal{V}$, given input $x$, '''inference''' produces output [[token (machine learning)|token]] sequence $y=(y_1,\cdots,y_T) \in \mathcal{V}^T$ chosen probabilistically:

$$
y\sim P_\theta(\cdot\mid x).
$$

{{Hidden example}}
With prompt $x=$ `"The capital of France is"`, 3 independent inferences with a typical, well-trained LLM may give:

$$
y^{(1)}=\texttt{"Paris."},\qquad
y^{(2)}=\texttt{"Paris, a city on the Seine."},\qquad
y^{(3)}=\texttt{"Lyon, argued some."}
$$
{{End hidden}}

=== Computational limitation ===

The globally most probable output sequence
$$
y^\star=\arg\max_{y\in\mathcal{V}^T}P_\theta(y\mid x)
$$

is calculated by a maximiser [[function]] over a space of size $|\mathcal{V}|^T \to \infty$, which cannot be enumerated for long sequences (large $T$). The output sequence must be generated sequentially in smaller steps (e.g., 1 to a few tokens).

=== Typical implementation: sequential next token prediction ===

[[File:Sequential next-token prediction.png|thumbnail|'''Sequential next token prediction''' starting with prompt <code>the</code> with ChatGPT3.]]
$$
\vec{z}_t=f_\theta\left(x,y_{1:t-1}\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{V}|},\\
y_t\sim\operatorname{Categorical}\left(\mathrm{softmax}\left(\vec{z}_t\right)\right).
$$

where $f_\theta$ is the model [[forward pass]] with [[model parameters]] $\theta$, and $\operatorname{Categorical(\cdot)}$ denotes the [[categorical distribution]] given probability vector $\cdot$.


<blockquote>
In '''sequential next token prediction''', the LLM first determines $y_1$ based on $x$, then determines $y_2$ based on $x,y_1$, $y_3$ based on $x,y_1,y_2$, so on so forth.
</blockquote>
